body:
Play is a fundamental aspect of human
development that continues all through our lives.
Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but
many individuals struggle to fully engage in these
spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often,
playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who cannot participate in the intended
manner ⓐfeeling excluded.
For children with disabilities, play is even more
crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social
skills. However, the conventional design of
playgrounds does not typically accommodate their
needs, either ⓑoverwhelm or boring them. A visit
to a standard playground with children with
disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design
ⓒthat fail to satisfy everyone.
Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and ⓓconnect with
nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging
design task. By involving children with disabilities
and their families in the design process and
creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge
ⓔthat play is more than just
a source
of
enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where
people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take
part in the joy of play.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael
Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed
playground. Unusual play structures and a large
ship provide (A)[endless / finite] experiences of play
that can engage every child. The various methods
of play have different means of access, allowing
kids who are able to scramble up hills, while
children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths
to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the
(B)[exclusive / inclusive] routes and elements of the
playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees
grants children and adults the chance to experience
the sensory aspects of plants.
Play isn’t just for kids anymore. (C)[Kid / Senior]
play spaces and public exercise equipment are
being installed around the world. Play spaces for
older adults provide health benefits and encourage
engagement with their families and community.
Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as
spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.
(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: finiteinclusive        Senior
endlessinclusive        Kid
finiteexclusive        Kid
endlessinclusive        Senior
endlessexclusive        Senior
solution: (A) 다양한 놀이 구조물과 큰 배가 모든 아이들이 참여할 수 있는 다양한 놀이 경험을 제공한다는 내용이므로 endless(무한 한)가 적절하다. (B) 걸을 수 있는 아이와 걸을 수 없는 아이 모두 이용할 수 있는 다양한 접근 경로를 설명하고 있으므로 inclusive(포괄적 인)가 적절하다. (C) 앞 문장에서 놀이가 더 이상 아이들만을 위한 것이 아니라 고 했고, 뒤에서 노인들을 위한 놀이 공간이 주는 이점과 모두 를 위한 공간으로서의 놀이터의 필요성을 언급하고 있으므로 Senior(노인)가 적절하다. 지학사(신상근) 1과

body:
Universal design suggests that design (A)be as
ⓐflexible as possible so that it can ⓑaccommodate
diverse needs and a wide range of individual
preferences. This could involve providing a variety
of options for ⓒcustomization or adding adjustable
features to a product.
Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse,
and the desk (B)picturing below. Do you notice how
they differ from the more common types of scissors,
mice, and desks? They are all designed for
left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the
world’s population, who are left-handed, (C)would
have found these simple products difficult to use.
The height-adjustable desk is also a good example
of a universal design that accommodates a wide
range of individual preferences and abilities. If the
desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it
to the heights they want. If desired, the user can
work while (D)standing. A wheelchair user is also
able to use the desk at a comfortable height.
Universal design also ensures (E)that an
environment or product is accessible to everyone.
Anyone should be able to use a design regardless
of who they are and what they’re capable of, and
no one should be ⓓexcluded. Curb cuts are a
good example. Without curb cuts, people in
wheelchairs would have a hard time ⓔnavigating
the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for
wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy
loads or (F)ride bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic
doors in public buildings also (G)allow all people to
enter without any major problems.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ flexible: able to bend or to be bent easily without
breaking
ⓑ accommodate: to provide someone with a place
to stay, live, or work
ⓒ customization: the action of making or changing
something according to the buyer's or user's needs
ⓓ exclude: to prevent someone or something from
taking part in an activity
ⓔ navigate: to find which way you need to go when
you are travelling from one place to another
solution: ⓒ 고객 맞춤: 구매자나 사용자의 요구에 따라 무언가를 만들 거나 변경하는 행위 ⓓ 배제하다: 누군가 또는 무언가가 어떤 활동에 참여하는 것을 막다 ⓔ 길을 찾다, 나아가다: 한 장소에서 다른 장소로 이동할 때 어떤 방향으로 가야 하는지를 찾다

body:
Universal design is not limited to the design of
physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes
for designs (A)[where / which] critical information is
conveyed well, ⓐ[depending on / regardless of] the
surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.
Information should be conveyed not just through
written language but also through ⓑ[universal /
exclusive] symbols and audio cues. For instance,
when it comes to foreign travelers, (B)[finding / find]
a restroom is much easier when they can simply
look for the universally recognized restroom symbol
rather than trying to interpret the local language. For
those with visual or audio impairments, bus and
subway arrival times are not only presented on
electronic boards but also called out through voice
announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates
the floor number, (C)[allowing / allows] individuals
with visual impairments to select their desired floor.
Additionally, audio announcements confirm the
selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator
has reached their desired floor.
As such, providing information in these ⓒ[diverse
/ uniform] forms ensures that everyone can access
and understand important information, regardless of
language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: depending on     universal  diverse
regardless of      universal  uniform
depending on     exclusive  uniform
regardless of      universal  diverse
regardless of      exclusive  diverse
solution: ⓐ 마지막 문장에서 언어 장벽, 감각 장애 등에 상관없이 모두 가 중요한 정보에 접근하고 이해할 수 있도록 보장한다고 했으 므로 ‘주변 환경이나 사용자의 감각 능력에 관계없이’라는 흐름 이 자연스럽다. 따라서 regardless of(~에 관계없이)가 적절하다. ⓑ 다음 문장의 예시에서 보편적으로 인식되는 화장실 기호를 간단히 찾을 수 있을 때 화장실을 찾기가 훨씬 더 쉽다고 했 으므로 ‘보편적인 기호와 오디오 신호를 통해’라는 흐름이 자 연스럽다. 따라서 universal(보편적인)이 적절하다. ⓒ 앞에서 여러 전달 방식(문자 언어, 보편적인 기호, 점자, 오 디오 신호 등)이 언급되었으므로 diverse(다양한)가 적절하다.

body:
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?

W: Hey, Danny. I didn’t know you ride a bike to
school.
M: Yeah. I’ve been riding for a while now. It helps
me keep in shape.
W: I’ve been thinking about doing the same, but
I’m worried about carrying a helmet everywhere.
M: I used to have the same problem, but I found
this foldable helmet.
W: You can fold your helmet? (A)Can you show me
how?
M: Sure. All I have to do is push both sides.
W: That’s convenient! I never knew such helmets
existed.
M: It’s a bit expensive, but it’s worth it.
choices: Can you guess how many times I fold it?
Do you mind if I tell you how to fold it?
Would you like to know how to fold it?
I wonder why you fold your helmet.
Can you tell me how to fold it?
solution: ‘Can you show me how?‘는 ‘방법을 알려 줄래?’라는 의미로, 설명을 요청할 때 쓰는 표현이며, 흐름상 헬멧을 어떻게 접는 지 묻고 있다. 따라서 ❺ ’Can you tell me how to fold it?(어 떻게 접는지 알려주시겠어요?)’로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

body:
W: Hello, everyone! Today, we’re excited to introduce
a new product (A)[designed / was designed] to
create a productive working environment. Say
goodbye to inconvenient desks and (B)[annoying
/ annoyed] backaches. Our height-adjustable desk
is the ultimate solution to address these
concerns. By simply pressing the button right
here on the side, you can effortlessly adjust the
height. It’s easy (C)[work / to work] with a more
comfortable posture. Experience a whole new,
elite level of productivity. Place your order right
now and relieve your backaches!

위 담화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: was designed       annoying     to work
designed      annoying     work
was designed       annoyed     work
designed      annoying     to work
designed      annoyed     to work
solution: (A) to introduce의 목적어인 a new product를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, 수식받는 명사구 a new product가 ‘고안된’ 대상이 므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 designed가 적절하다. (B) 명사 backaches(허리 통증)를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, backaches가 ‘성가시게 하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미인 현재 분사 annoying이 적절하다. (C) 가주어 It에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로 to부정사 to work가 적절하다.

body:
Universal design also ensures that an environment
or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should
be able to use a design regardless of who they are
and what they’re capable of, and no one should be
excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without
curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard
time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers
not only for wheelchair users but also for people
moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts,
automatic doors in public buildings also allow all
people to enter without any major problems.
Another characteristic of universal design is
requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks
to create products that can be used efficiently and
comfortably without (A)[cause / causing] unnecessary
fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble
trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck.
Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people
with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand
or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever
opening devices have been designed. A lever-type
door handle, which requires no firm grip or
twisting, is also an example (B)[that / what] reflects
this characteristic of universal design. A door with a
lever-type door handle can be opened (C)[using /
used] an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits
people carrying baskets as well as those with
limited strength in their hands.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: causing that     using
causing what     using
cause what     used
causing that     used
cause that     using
solution: (A) 전치사 without의 목적어 자리이며, 뒤에 명사구 unnecessary fatigue가 이어지므로 목적어를 취할 수 있는 능동형 동명사 causing이 적절하다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(reflects ~ design)을 이끌어 선행 사 an example을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (C) 완전한 절(A door ~ opened)에 접속사나 주어 없이 이어 지며 주절의 동작(can be opened)과 ‘팔꿈치나 오므린 손을 사용하는 것(using an elbow or a closed hand)‘이 동시에 일 어나는 부대상황을 나타내므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리 이다. 뒤에 목적어(an elbow or a closed hand)가 이어지므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 using이 적절하다.

solution: (B) picturing → pictured (명사구 the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk가 ‘사진에 보이는’ 대상이므로 picturing을 수동의 의미를 갖는 pictured로 고친다. 참고로 pictured 앞에 ‘주격 관계대명사+be동사’ that[which]are가 생 략된 것으로 볼 수 있다.) (C) would have found → would find (without은 ‘~이 없다면’ 의 의미로, 주절에는 단순 조건문, 가정법과거, 가정법 과거완 료 모두 사용 가능한데, 흐름상 ‘그것들이 없다면’이라는 현재 사실의 반대를 가정하는 것이므로 ’without ~, 주어+과거조동 사+동사원형 … (~이 없다면 …할 것이다)’의 가정법 과거가 쓰 여야 한다. 따라서 would have found를 would find로 고친다.) What do you think good design is? Some might
assert good design makes products easy to use,
while others might say ⓐwhat good design is
stylish or innovative. There are even some who
believe that good design should be as
environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are
important elements of design. However, there is a
new idea called “universal design.” This idea
suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty
looks and functions. Universal design takes into
account the diverse needs of different people and
includes features that make it possible for them
ⓑaccess and use products without any barriers.
Now let’s take a look at how universal design is
tackling the problem of limited access and
reshaping the design of products and services.
Universal design is not limited to the design of
physical products or facilities. Universal design
pushes for designs ⓒwhich critical information is
conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.
Information should be conveyed not just through
written language but also through universal symbols
and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to
foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier
when they can simply look for the universally
recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to
interpret the local language. For those with visual
or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times
are not only presented on electronic boards but
also called out through voice announcements. In
elevators, braille, ⓓthat indicates the floor number,
allows individuals with visual impairments to select
their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements
confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when
the elevator has reached their desired floor.
As such, providing information in these diverse
forms ⓔensure that everyone can access and
understand important information, regardless of
language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.
Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With
universal design, no one needs to put up with
unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal
design suggest that it should be part of every
design. Take a look around you. Is there anything
that needs improvement so that it can be
accessible to more people? If so, why not create a
design and bring joy to more people?

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ: what → that
ⓑ: access and use → accessing and using
ⓒ: which → in which
ⓓ: that → which
ⓔ: ensure → ensures
solution: ⓑ access and use → to access and (to) use (동사 make, 가목 적어 it, 목적격보어 possible, 의미상 주어 for them과 함께 ‘-가 ~하는 것을 …하게 만들다’의 의미를 갖는 ‘make+it(가목적어)+목 적격보어(형용사)+for+의미상 주어+to부정사(진목적어)’의 구조로, ‘가목적어-진목적어’ 구문을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 진목적어 자리 이자 ‘for+목적어(them)‘의 형태로 의미상주어를 취하고 있으므로, access and use를 accessing and using이 아니라 to부정사구 to access and (to) use로 고친다. 참고로 to부정사가 병렬 연결될 때 to는 생략 가능하므로 to use 또는 use 모두 가능하다.)

Play is a fundamental aspect of human

that play is more than just a source of enjoyment.

abilities, ages, and languages can take part in the
joy of play.

For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground. Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child. The various methods of play have different means of access, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants.
Play isn’t just for kids anymore. Senior play spaces and public exercise equipment are being installed around the world. Play spaces for older adults provide health benefits and encourage engagement with their families and community. Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.

Another characteristic of universal design is
ⓐrequiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks
to create products ⓑwhat can be used efficiently and
comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue.
Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to
open a lid of a jar that was stuck. ⓒOpening a lid can
be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the
elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments.
Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been
designed. A lever-type door handle, ⓓthat requires no
firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this
characteristic of universal design. A door with a
lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or
a closed hand, which ⓔbenefits people carrying baskets
as well as those with limited strength in their hands.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?

(A) Universal design completely eliminates the need
for any physical effort when opening products
like jars or doors. (T/F)
(B) People with weak grip strength or hand-related
difficulties may struggle to open a tightly
closed jar. (T/F)
(C) Products with universal design are unnecessary
for general users. (T/F)
(D) A lever-type door handle can be operated without
requiring users to firmly hold or twist it. (T/F)
(E) People carrying baskets may find a lever-type
door handle useful because they can open the
door with an elbow or a closed hand. (T/F)

flexible as possible so that it can accommodate
diverse needs and a wide range of individual
preferences. This could involve providing a variety
of options for customization or adding adjustable
features to a product.
Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse,
and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how
they differ from the more common types of
scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for
left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of
the world’s population, who are left-handed, would
find these simple products difficult to use.

of a universal design that accommodates a wide
range of individual preferences and abilities. If the
desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it
to the heights they want. If desired, the user can
work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able
to use the desk at a comfortable height.

Universal design is not limited to the design of
physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes
for designs in which critical information is conveyed
well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the
user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed
not just through written language but also through
universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when
it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is
much easier when they can simply look for the
universally recognized restroom symbol rather than
trying to interpret the local language. For those with
visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival
times are not only presented on electronic boards but
also called out through voice announcements. In
elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number,
allows individuals with visual impairments to select
their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements
confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when
the elevator has reached their desired floor.
As such, providing information in these diverse forms
ensures that ______________________________________________.
Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With
universal design, no one needs to put up with
unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal
design suggest that it should be part of every
design. Take a look around you. Is there anything
that needs improvement so that it can be
accessible to more people? If so, why not create a
design and bring joy to more people?

False Bananas

20 million people (A)[rely on / do without] this

Dr. Perry: Yes, indeed. Most of the original taste
tests (A)[has yielded / have yielded] positive
reviews. Many taste testers were unable to
taste a difference between lab-grown and
regular meat. Some of them even guessed
incorrectly which sample was lab-grown.
Host: I see, but why do we need lab-grown meat
when we already have plant-based meat?
Dr. Perry: Plant-based meat has come a long way,
but some people still feel that it does not
quite match the taste, texture, and overall
eating experience of real animal meat.
Lab-grown meat can provide people with a
product that is biologically identical to real
meat in a way that’s much less harmful to
the planet and animals.
Host: Very well. I think people interested in the
idea of lab-grown meat will also wonder
(B)[what / if] it’s safe.
Dr. Perry: Lab-grown chicken was first approved in
Singapore in 2020, and more recently, the
U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the
U.S. Department of Agriculture have also
approved the sale of lab-grown chicken.
These facts demonstrate that lab-grown meat
is probably safe. It’s hoped that the safety of
cultured meat will improve with the
development of technology. Of course, as
with all food products, we will need to
collect more data over a long period of time
(C)[to ensure / ensure] its safety.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: has yieldedwhatensure
has yieldedifto ensure
have yieldedwhatto ensure
have yieldedifto ensure
have yieldedifensure
solution: (A) most of+명사(구)’가 주어 자리에 올 때 동사의 수는 of 뒤 명사(구)에 수일치 시킨다. 따라서 주어 ‘Most of the original taste tests’에서 of 뒤에 복수명사구 the original taste tests’가 쓰였으므로, 복수동사 have yielded가 알맞다. (B) 동사 wonder의 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 절을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘~인지’라는 뜻을 갖는 명사절 접속사 if가 알맞다. (C) 문장의 동사로 will need가 있으므로 준동사 자리이며 ’보 장하기 위해‘라는 뜻으로 이어지므로, 목적(~하기 위해)을 나타 내는 to부정사 to ensure가 알맞다.

solution: (A) 비교급 형용사구 less harmful 앞에서 ‘훨씬’이라는 뜻으로 이를 강조할 수 있는 부사 much가 알맞다. (B) 뒤에 동사구 will (also) wonder가 있으므로 주절의 동사 think의 목적어가 절의 형태로 이어짐을 알 수 있으며, 목적어 절의 주어인 명사 people을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 와야 한다. 따라서 people이 ‘관심을 가지게 된’ 대상이므로 수 동을 나타내는 과거분사 interested가 알맞다. As our planet faces increasing environmental
challenges and climate change, there is growing
interest in eco-friendly foods ⓐthat have less
impact on the environment. The following foods
eaten in various regions of the world ⓑare gaining
attention as (A)_______________________________________.
False Bananas
Ethiopia, noted for its coffee cultivation, is also a
region ⓒwhich the promising future crop enset
prevails. Enset, also known as “false banana,” is a
close relative of the banana. The fruit of the plant
isn’t safe to eat, but the stems and roots can be
processed and used ⓓto making bread.
Approximately 20 million people rely on this plant
for food in Ethiopia, but it is almost unknown
outside of the country. Scientists anticipate that this
crop has the potential to feed more than 100
million people in a warming world, ⓔestablished
itself as a new fundamental food for the future.
Cacti
ⓕNative to the deserts of both North and South
America, cacti are a fundamental food in Latin
American communities, where the flat pads are
often stirred and served with eggs or in salads and
tacos. There are over 1,500 species of cacti, and
many of them are safe to eat. Cacti are rich in
fiber, vitamins, and other nutrients. Cacti’s ability to
thrive in dry and harsh environments ⓖmake them
a crucial crop in the face of climate change.

다음 글의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?

Dr. Perry: Lab-grown meat refers to meat grown
from cells we keep alive in a controlled
environment. It is different from conventional
beef or chicken, which is produced by raising
and slaughtering farm animals. It’s also different from plant-based meat, which
derives its protein solely from plants. It is
often called cultured or cultivated meat, too.
Host: I’m sure many people are wondering about
the reasons for developing lab-grown meat.
Dr. Perry: Every year, 80 billion animals are slaughtered
for meat. The livestock industry uses 83% of
the world’s farming land and produces 60%
of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions.
Since lab-grown meat doesn’t require killing
animals, it reduces carbon emissions, and it
retains the same nutrition and flavor as regular
meat. This makes it an attractive substitute.

to assess the long-term safety of cultivatedmeat consumption
to emphasize the nutritional superiority ofconventional meat
to compare the production methods of cultivatedand conventional meat
to explain the concept of cultivated meat andthe need for its development

body:
Host: Plant-based meat is available in many stores
and restaurants. When could we expect to
see lab-grown meat on grocery store shelves?
Dr. Perry: Lab-grown meat has gotten much
cheaper than it used to be, but it is still
more expensive than conventional meat. This
high price is an issue that needs to be
resolved for the popularization of cultured
meat. Several food companies have been
working on finding less expensive production
methods, so it won’t be long before you
can buy it in grocery stores.
Host: I see your point. Do you have any final
comments for our viewers?
Dr. Perry: The idea of eating meat produced in a
lab might seem gross to some people, but I
believe (A)we need to have an open mind for
our future. It’s an excellent alternative to
producing meat in the traditional way.
Host: Dr. Perry, thank you for answering our
questions about meat grown in labs.
According to one survey, 80% of U.S.
consumers report that they would be likely
to try cultivated meat. Are you one of them?
Thank you for watching. Good night.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

how to reduce the production costs of lab-grownmeat
the cost barrier and future potential of lab-grownmeat
strategies for selling lab-grown meat in grocerystores
solution: 배양육은 가격이 여전히 높지만, 식품 회사들의 저비용 생산 노력 으로 곧 식료품점에서 판매되어 전통적인 방식으로 고기를 생산 하는 것에 대한 훌륭한 대안이 될 것이라고 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ❹ ‘배양육의 비용 장벽과 미래 잠재력’이 알맞다.

body:
Seaweed
Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety of
dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks. Seaweed
is mostly eaten in Korea, Japan, and China, but it is
becoming more common in other parts of the world.
Seaweed, gaining attention for addressing soil
degradation, is packed with fiber, essential vitamins,
and minerals, offering numerous health benefits.
Insects
Insects have been a traditional source of protein in
many cultures for centuries. (A) People have been
enjoying seasoned, roasted insects for a long time
in Mexico, and many African countries incorporate
insects into soups. (B) Insects are high in protein,
vitamins, and minerals. (C) In contrast to other
protein sources, they also require significantly less
land, water, and food to produce, which diminishes
the environmental footprint of our diets. (D) These
merits make insects a magnificent alternative,
sustainable source of protein. (E)

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the cultural differences in consuming seaweedand insects across various regions
the challenges of introducing seaweed andinsects into modern food systems
seaweed and insects as sustainable alternativesto conventional agricultural products
the changing public perception of seaweed andinsects as unconventional food choices
the nutritional value of seaweed and insects andtheir potential as eco-friendly food sources

body:
Host: Welcome to News Tonight. ⓐThat was once
the stuff of science fiction is finally arriving
on our dinner plates. We’re talking about
lab-grown meat. You may be reluctant ⓑto
try it. However ⓒstrangely it may seem, many
people say it tastes just like regular meat,
and it has big advantages for preventing
animal suffering and reducing pollution.
Today, we have tissue engineering expert Dr.
Mike Perry with us to learn more about
lab-grown meat. It’s an honor to meet you,
Dr. Perry. Can you tell our viewers what kind
of research you are currently conducting?
Dr. Perry: Thank you for having me, Kelly. I am
currently leading a lab-grown meat project
research team. Our team is working to trace
the process of cell division and growth in
lab-grown meat, with the goal of discovering
a cultivation environment that ⓓenables the
creation of a better texture while burning
less energy.
Host: I see. Now let’s dive into our main topic,
lab-grown meat. First, tell us ⓔwhat lab-grown

along rocky coasts around the world. This plant

(B) 주어인 AI disease diagnostic programs와 동사구 may accurately diagnose 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이끌어야 하며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(are already used in many hospitals)이 이어져 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로, 계속적 용법으로 관계대명사 that은 쓸 수 없다.

body:
Strong AI and Weak AI are two fascinating branches of artificial intelligence that capture our imagination. Strong AI, like something from a sci-fi movie, can think, learn, and perform various tasks and cope with various situations just like humans. The current level of AI systems cannot do such things yet. Weak AI, on the other hand, the kind we now encounter daily, focuses on conducting one job well. It can do things such as recommending movies, giving us directions, or even helping us pick the perfect songs. However, it ⓐoutperforms humans only in the specific tasks it is designed for, and it operates under far more constraints than even the most basic human intelligence. There are several differences between Weak AI and Strong AI.
What Is Weak AI?
Did you know that the computer playing chess and the helpful voice assistant on your phone are both examples of Weak AI? They may be impressive, but they’re designed for specific tasks and can’t handle anything outside their programming. Weak AI is a category of artificial intelligence ⓑconfined to a finite domain. By performing operations that require considerable time and utilizing methods that are not always accessible to people, this technology can be advantageous to society.
It concentrates on tasks such as responding to user input searches or playing games. While it is only as good as its programming and training, Weak AI still helps convert enormous amounts of data into useful information by ⓒidentifying patterns and generating predictions.
What Is Strong AI?
Strong AI is designed to mimic the cognitive abilities of a human being. It is called “strong” because it has the potential to perform a wide range of tasks, rather than being limited to a specific set of tasks. (A)인공지능 시스템이 우리의 모든 지능, 감정, 폭넓은 지식을 가지고 인간의 능력들에 더 많이 접근할수록, 그 인공지능 시스템은 ‘더 강하다’고 여겨진다.
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI is that it is designed to learn and ⓓavoid new situations. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system designed to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is that it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is ⓔpossible to create Strong AI in the future.

body:
Before the Internet, people with vast (A)[wealth / knowledge] were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he would probably (B)[win / lose] by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to (C)[elicit / provide] the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context in which you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. ⓐ우리는 현재 모든 세부 사항들이 암기되도록 하는 것보다 정보를 활용하는 능력이 더 중요한 시대에 있다. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.

(A) / (B) / (C)
choices: wealth / win / elicit
knowledge / win / provide
knowledge / lose / provide
wealth / lose / provide
knowledge / lose / elicit
solution:
(A) 어려운 문제가 나오는 퀴즈 쇼가 매우 인기 있었으며, 이제는 인공지능의 존재로 인해 많은 사람들이 왜 그런 정보를 암기해야 하는지 의문을 갖는다는 내용이 이어지므로, 인터넷 이전에는 방대한 지식을 가진 사람들이 가장 재능 있는 사람들로 여겨졌다는 흐름이 되는 knowledge(지식)가 알맞다.
(B) 2011년 인기 있는 미국의 퀴즈 쇼에서 74번 우승한 적이 있는 사람이 슈퍼컴퓨터와 대결했으며, 컴퓨터가 완승을 거둔 결과는 인간이 사실적 정보를 찾는 데 있어서 컴퓨터를 따라갈 수 없다는 것을 보여준다고 했으므로, 만약 그 사람이 현재의 인공지능과 대결한다면 아마도 더 큰 차이로 질 것이라는 흐름이 되는 lose(지다)가 알맞다.
(C) 우리가 아무리 열심히 노력한다 해도 방대한 양의 정보를 외우는 데 있어서 인공지능에 필적할 수 없다고 한 뒤, 우리가 집중해야 할 것은 인공지능으로부터 ‘올바른’ 답을 얻는 것이라고 했으므로, 그 핵심은 인공지능으로부터 원하는 답을 이끌어내기 위해 올바른 질문을 하는 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 elicit(~을 이끌어내다)이 알맞다.

Objectively evaluating others’ conditions without emotional involvement
Deliberately relying on automated systems to handle patients’ emotional stress
Actually prioritizing emotional detachment over compassionate care when treating patients

body:
Strong AI and Weak AI are two fascinating branches of artificial intelligence that capture our imagination. Strong AI, like something from a sci-fi movie, can think, learn, and perform various tasks and cope with various situations just like humans. The current level of AI systems cannot do such things yet. Weak AI, on the other hand, the kind we now encounter daily, (A)[focus / focuses] on conducting one job well. It can do things such as recommending movies, giving us directions, or even helping us pick the perfect songs. However, it outperforms humans only in the specific tasks it is designed for, and it operates under far more constraints than even the most basic human intelligence. There are several differences between Weak AI and Strong AI.
What Is Weak AI?
Did you know that the computer playing chess and the helpful voice assistant on your phone are both examples of Weak AI? They may be impressive, but they’re designed for specific tasks and can’t handle anything outside their programming. Weak AI is a category of artificial intelligence confined to a finite domain. By performing operations that require considerable time and utilizing methods that are not always accessible to people, this technology can be advantageous to society.
It concentrates on tasks such as responding to user input searches or playing games. While it is only as good as its programming and training, Weak AI still helps convert enormous amounts of data into useful information by identifying patterns and (B)[generate / generating] predictions.
What Is Strong AI?
Strong AI is designed to mimic the cognitive abilities of a human being. It is called “strong” because it has the potential (C)[perform / to perform] a wide range of tasks, rather than being limited to a specific set of tasks. The more an AI system approaches the abilities of a human being, with all our intelligence, emotion, and broad knowledge, the “stronger” the AI system is considered.
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI is that it is designed to learn and adapt to new situations. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system designed to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is that it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is possible to create Strong AI in the future.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: focuses generating perform
focus generate perform
focuses generating to perform
focuses generate to perform
focus generating to perform
solution:
(A) 단수명사구인 주어 Weak AI에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로, 단수동사 focuses가 알맞다. 주어와 동사 사이에 부사구 on the other hand와 주어를 부연 설명하는 동격 어구인 the kind we now encounter daily가 삽입되어 있다.
(B) 전치사 by의 목적어 자리에서 동명사 identifying과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 동명사구를 이루어야 하므로, 동명사 generating이 알맞다.
(C) 문장의 동사로 has가 있으므로 준동사가 올 자리이고, 흐름상 ‘수행할’이라는 의미로 명사구 the potential을 수식하는 형용사구를 이루어야 하므로, 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to perform이 알맞다.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the biggest catch phrases these days. While cutting-edge technology might have benefits for many people, it is also a cause of concern for those ⓐtry to start a career. With so many jobs disappearing, what kind of career should you pursue, and what skills should you have to survive in the AI age? Whether you like it or hate it, AI technology is probably here to stay. Here are the core competencies you need to foster for a great career in the age of AI.
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle ⓑbuilt by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he ⓒwill probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and ⓓhowever hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context ⓔwhere you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell ⓕhow accurately the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ try → trying 또는 who are trying ⓒ will → would
ⓕ how accurately → how accurate

(C) 인공지능을 두려워하기보다 그것을 이 새로운 시대의 동반자로 받아들여야 한다는 내용과 접속사 and(그리고)로 연결되어 있으므로 인공지능과 협업하고 인공지능을 보완할 방법을 찾아야 한다는 흐름의 complement(~을 보완하다)가 알맞다.

body:
According to a future job report published by a top global investment bank, up to 300 million jobs around the world could be affected by artificial intelligence. The report also noted that technological innovation has historically created employment growth in the long run. In the age of AI, the ability ⓐto adapt to new technologies and work environments is crucial. You must (A)[resist / welcome] change and be open to learning and ⓑmastering new skills. It is very likely that many of those without AI skills will ⓒbe left behind. That is why we must become life-long learners.
(B)[Continuous / Sporadic] upskilling and reskilling will enable you to stay valuable in the changing job market. AI will replace some jobs but substantially alter ⓓmuch more. Furthermore, you probably won’t be replaced by AI. More likely a person with AI skills will replace you.
In conclusion, surviving and competing with AI ⓔrequire a shift in mindset. Instead of fearing AI, we must embrace it as a companion in this new era and find ways to collaborate with it and (C)[complement / undermine] it. We must also focus on developing interpersonal skills ⓕthat machines cannot replace. By doing so, we can not only survive in this era of AI but also thrive and prosper.
윗글의 첫 번째 문단과 두 번째 문단의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: How Technological Innovation Has Created Jobs over Time
Stay Competitive Through Life-Long Learning in the AI Era
The Significance of Choosing Occupations Unaffected by AI
Replace Traditional Classroom Education with AI-Based Instruction
The Necessity of Restricting Technological Innovation to Protect Existing Jobs
solution: 인공지능이 일자리와 고용 환경에 영향을 미침에 따라 새로운 기술과 업무 환경의 변화를 수용하고, 새로운 기술을 배우고 숙달하는 평생 학습자가 되어야 하며 또한 지속적인 기능 향상과 재교육을 통해 변화하는 직업 시장에서 자신의 가치를 유지해야 한다는 내용의 글이므로, 글의 제목으로 ❷ ‘AI 시대에 평생 학습을 통해 경쟁력을 유지하라’가 알맞다.

body:
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he would probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context in which you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.
In the age of AI, using information matters more than (A)______ it, so we need to understand the context and have some prior knowledge of the topic to ask the right questions, and then check the (B)______ of AI’s answers.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: retaining    clarity
collecting    completeness
organizing    correctness
summarizing    relevance
memorizing    accuracy
solution:
[요약문] AI 시대에는 정보를 (A)암기하는 것보다 활용하는 것이 더 중요하므로, 우리는 적절한 질문을 하기 위해 질문의 맥락을 이해하고 그 주제에 관한 배경지식을 어느 정도 갖추어야 하며, 다음으로 AI 답변의 (B)정확성을 확인해야 한다.
오답
① 기억하는 것 명확성
② 모으는 것 완전함
③ 정리하는 것 정확함
④ 요약하는 것 관련성

body:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the biggest catch phrases these days. While cutting-edge technology might have benefits for many people, it is also a cause of concern for those trying to start a career. With so many jobs disappearing, what kind of career should you pursue, and what skills should you have to survive in the AI age? Whether you like it or hate it, AI technology is probably here to stay. Here are the core competencies you need to foster for a great career in the age of AI.

다음 글의 바로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: ways to cultivate the competencies needed for a successful career in the pre-digital era
major policies designed to protect workers from unemployment in an AI-driven economy
the financial benefits companies can gain by replacing human employees with AI systems
the growing demand for professionals specializing in the design and maintenance of AI systems
specific capabilities that can help individuals build rewarding professional lives in an AI-driven age
solution:
인공지능(AI)은 요즘 가장 주목을 끄는 유행어 중 하나로, 아주 많은 직업이 사라지고 있는 상황에서 인공지능 시대에서 살아남기 위해 어떤 종류의 직업을 추구해야 하고 어떤 능력이 있어야 하는가에 대해 질문하며 인공지능 시대에 훌륭한 경력을 쌓기 위해 길러야 할 핵심 역량을 소개하겠다고 예고하고 있으므로, 주어진 글 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 ⑤ ‘인공지능이 주도하는 시대에 개인들이 가치 있는 직업 생활을 구축하도록 도울 수 있는 구체적인 능력들’이 알맞다.
오답
① 디지털 이전 시대에서 성공적인 직업을 위해 필요한 역량들을 기른 방법들
② 인공지능이 주도하는 경제에서 노동자들을 실업으로부터 보호하기 위해 고안된 주요 정책들
③ 기업들이 인간 직원들을 인공지능 시스템으로 대체함으로써 얻을 수 있는 재정적 이익들
④ 인공지능 시스템의 설계와 유지를 전문으로 하는 전문가들에 대한 증가하는 수요

body:
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge ⓐwere considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why ⓑone would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. (A)컴퓨터가 압도적인 승리를 거두었다는 사실은 인간이 사실적 정보를 찾는 데 있어서 컴퓨터들을 따라갈 수 없다는 것을 보여준다. If that person were to compete with current AI, he ⓒwill probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and ⓓno matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context ⓔwhich you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do ⓕwhat AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓒ will → would (If절에 were to가 쓰였으며, if절과 주절이 모두 실현 가능성이 전혀 없는 일을 가정해야 하므로, ‘If+주어+were to+동사원형 ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …(~이라면, …일 텐데)’ 형태의 가정법 과거를 이루도록 조동사 will을 would로 고친다.)
ⓔ which → in which 또는 where (완전한 절(you’re ~ question)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the context를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사 which를 장소의 관계부사 where 또는 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 사용한 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태인 in which로 고친다. 참고로, 물리적인 장소뿐 아니라 추상적 의미의 장소를 나타내는 선행사 뒤에도 관계부사 where를 쓸 수 있다.)
*원래 지문에는 in which가 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 부사구 Before the Internet(인터넷 이전에)이 나타내는 과거에 주어(people with vast knowledge)가 ‘여겨졌던’ 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘consider+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …인 것으로 여기다)’의 to부정사구(to be ~ talented)가 이어져 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be considered+(to be+)보어(~가 …인 것으로 여겨지다)’를 써야 한다. 따라서 주어의 핵심인 복수명사 people에 수일치한 복수동사 were를 쓴 과거시제 수동태 were considered는 알맞다.
ⓑ 타동사로 쓰인 question(~에 의문을 가지다)의 목적어인 why 이하는 ‘의문사+평서문’의 어순이 되어야 하므로, 의문사 why 뒤에 ‘(일반적인) 사람’을 뜻하는 대명사 주어 one과 조동사 would, 동사원형 memorize가 차례로 쓰인 one would memorize는 알맞다.
ⓓ ’아무리 ~하더라도‘라는 뜻으로 ’no matter how+형용사/부사+주어+동사~‘를 사용할 수 있으므로, 동사 try를 수식하는 부사 hard를 이용한 no matter how hard는 알맞다.
ⓕ 전치사 at의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(AI is not good at)을 이끌어 동사 do의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함해 ’~한 것‘을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what은 알맞다.

body:
AI can often find the information we want quickly, but there are problems with this. AI creates a lot of false or biased information. Further, AI cannot understand the intentions of the person who created the information, nor does it have the ability to judge whether the information is right or wrong.
(A) The proportion of male employees was very high and thus the AI’s machine learning had an underlying bias towards male data. When analyzing the information provided by AI, it is always necessary to assess the quality of information — remember: garbage in, garbage out.
(B) Moreover, stories of AI providing fake information are often reported. For example, there was a case of a lawyer who submitted non-existent cases made by AI to a real court. There has also been an example of AI recommending restaurants that didn’t exist.
(C) Just as much as misleading information, feeding biased information into AI causes incorrect or even harmful output. A world-famous Internet company had AI study ten years of employee records to create a new employee selection algorithm. However, the company decided not to use the algorithm when it favored men over women.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 인공지능(AI)이 틀리거나 편향된 정보를 많이 만들어내고 정보가 옳은지 그른지를 판단할 능력도 없다는 문제점을 언급하는 주어진 글 다음에, Moreover(더욱이)를 사용해 인공지능이 가짜 정보를 제공한다는 기사가 자주 보도된다는 사실을 덧붙이고, 그 예로 인공지능이 만든 존재하지 않는 사건을 실제 법원에 제출한 변호사의 사례와 인공지능이 존재하지 않는 음식점을 추천한 사례를 제시한 (B), 앞서 다룬 오해의 소지가 있는 정보만큼이나 편향된 정보도 해로운 결과를 초래한다는 또 다른 측면을 언급하며 10년간의 직원 기록을 연구한 인공지능이 남성을 선호한 사례를 제시하는 (C), 인공지능이 남성을 선호한 원인에 대해 남성 직원의 비율이 높아 인공지능의 머신 러닝이 남성 데이터에 대한 근본적인 편향을 가지고 있었다고 설명하며, 인공지능이 제공한 정보를 분석할 때 정보의 질을 평가하는 것이 항상 필요하다는 결론을 제시하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:

Further, AI cannot understand the intentions of the person who created the information, nor does it have the ability to judge whether the information is right or wrong.
(A) The proportion of male employees was very high and thus the AI’s machine learning had an underlying bias towards male data. When analyzing the information provided by AI, it is always necessary to assess the quality of information — remember: garbage in, garbage out.
(B) Moreover, stories of AI providing fake information are often reported. For example, there was a case of a lawyer who submitted non-existent cases made by AI to a real court. There has also been an example of AI recommending restaurants that didn’t exist.
(C) Just as much as misleading information, feeding biased information into AI causes incorrect or even harmful output. A world-famous Internet company had AI study ten years of employee records to create a new employee selection algorithm. However, the company decided not to use the algorithm when it favored men over women.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Need for Careful Assessment of AI-Provided information
Why AI-Created Information Requires Less Human Intervention
How AI Eliminates Human Bias in Generating Reliable Information
The Gradual Improvement in the Accuracy of AI-Based Information Systems
The Necessity for AI Systems That Evaluate Information Fairly and Rapidly
solution:
인공지능이 정보를 빠르게 찾을 수 있다는 장점이 있지만, 틀리거나 편향된 정보를 만들어내 해로운 결과를 초래할 수 있다는 문제점과 사례를 다룬 뒤 인공지능이 제공한 정보를 분석할 때 정보의 질을 평가하는 것이 항상 필요하다는 주장을 제시하므로, 글의 제목으로 ① ‘인공지능에 의해 제공된 정보에 대한 신중한 평가의 필요성’이 알맞다.
오답
② 인공지능에 의해 만들어진 정보가 더 적은 인간의 개입을 필요로 하는 이유
③ 인공지능이 신뢰할 수 있는 정보를 생성하는 데 있어 인간의 편향을 제거하는 방식
④ 인공지능 기반 정보 시스템의 정확성의 점진적인 향상
⑤ 정보를 공정하고 신속하게 평가하는 인공지능 시스템의 필요성

body:
It is AI that is good at collecting and classifying information. Meanwhile, it is humans that are best at dealing with people. The ability to ______ is potentially the most important human ability that artificial intelligence cannot replace. For example, AI disease diagnostic programs, which are already used in many hospitals, may accurately diagnose a patient’s illness such as cancer, but they don’t have the human touch that can make eye contact, empathize with pain, share worries, hold hands, or give encouragement to patients in despair. It is human doctors who can cure the patient’s emotional distress. Actually knowing and caring about what others think and feel is a unique competitive advantage we still possess.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: diagnose diseases through advanced computational analysis
maintain professional distance to evaluate human suffering
understand others, share their feelings, and connect emotionally
figure out others’ thoughts to predict and control their behavior
improve medical accuracy by minimizing direct contact with patients
solution:
정보를 수집하고 분류하는 데 능숙한 것은 인공지능이지만 사람을 가장 잘 상대하는 것은 인간이라고 한 뒤, 예를 들어 인공지능 질병 진단 프로그램은 환자와 눈을 맞추거나, 고통에 공감하며 고민을 나누는 것과 같은 인간적인 손길이 없다고 말하며, 다른 사람이 생각하고 느끼는 것을 실제로 알고 마음을 쓰는 것은 우리가 여전히 가진 고유한 경쟁 우위라고 설명하므로, 다른 사람들에 대한 이해와 정서적 소통 능력이 인공지능이 대체할 수 없는 인간의 가장 중요한 능력이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ ‘다른 사람들을 이해하고, 그들의 감정을 공유하며, 정서적으로 연결되다’가 알맞다.
본문변형 빈칸은 원래 ‘understand, empathize, and communicate with people emotionally’였음
오답
① 고급 계산 분석을 통해 질병을 진단하다
② 인간의 고통을 평가하기 위해 전문적인 거리를 유지하다
④ 다른 사람들의 행동을 예측하고 통제하기 위해 그들의 생각을 알아내다
⑤ 환자와의 직접적인 접촉을 최소화함으로써 의학적 정확성을 향상시키다

body:
According to a future job report published by a top global investment bank, up to 300 million jobs around the world could be affected by artificial intelligence. The report also noted ⓐ[that / what] technological innovation has historically created employment growth in the long run. (A) In the age of AI, the ability to adapt to new technologies and work environments is crucial. (B) You must embrace change and be open to learning and mastering new skills. (C) Once individuals acquire the skills required for their current jobs, further learning becomes excessive. (D) It is very likely that many of those without AI skills will be left behind. (E) That is why we must become life-long learners.
Continuous upskilling and reskilling will enable you ⓑ[stay / to stay] valuable in the changing job market. AI will replace some jobs but substantially alter many more. Furthermore, you probably won’t be replaced by AI. More likely a person with AI skills will replace you.
In conclusion, surviving and competing with AI requires a shift in mindset. Instead of fearing AI, we must embrace it as a companion in this new era and ⓒ[find / finding] ways to collaborate with it and complement it. We must also focus on developing interpersonal skills that machines cannot replace. By doing so, we can not only survive in this era of AI but also thrive and prosper.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 인공지능의 시대에는 새로운 기술과 작업 환경에 적응하는 능력이 중요하고, 변화를 수용하며 새로운 기술을 배우고 숙달하는 데 열려 있어야 하고, 인공지능 기술이 없는 이들은 뒤처질 가능성이 매우 크므로 평생 학습자가 되어야 한다는 흐름이므로, 개인이 계속 배워야 한다는 글의 주장과 대비되는 내용인 (C) ‘개인들이 자신의 현재 직업에 필요한 기술을 일단 습득하면, 추가적인 학습은 과도해진다.’는 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
According to a future job report published by a top global investment bank, up to 300 million jobs around the world could be affected by artificial intelligence. The report also noted ⓐ[that / what] technological innovation has historically created employment growth in the long run. (A) In the age of AI, the ability to adapt to new technologies and work environments is crucial. (B) You must embrace change and be open to learning and mastering new skills. (C) Once individuals acquire the skills required for their current jobs, further learning becomes excessive. (D) It is very likely that many of those without AI skills will be left behind. (E) That is why we must become life-long learners.
Continuous upskilling and reskilling will enable you ⓑ[stay / to stay] valuable in the changing job market. AI will replace some jobs but substantially alter many more. Furthermore, you probably won’t be replaced by AI. More likely a person with AI skills will replace you.
In conclusion, surviving and competing with AI requires a shift in mindset. Instead of fearing AI, we must embrace it as a companion in this new era and ⓒ[find / finding] ways to collaborate with it and complement it. We must also focus on developing interpersonal skills that machines cannot replace. By doing so, we can not only survive in this era of AI but also thrive and prosper.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: that / to stay / finding
what / to stay / find
that / stay / find
that / to stay / find
what / stay / finding
solution:
ⓐ 동사 noted의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(technological ~ run)을 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사 enable은 ‘~가 …할 수 있게 하다’라는 뜻의 5형식 구문(enable+목적어+목적격보어)에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 to부정사 to stay가 알맞다.
ⓒ 조동사 must 뒤의 동사원형 embrace와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, 동사원형 find가 알맞다.

body:
Weak AI, on the other hand, the kind we now encounter daily, focuses on conducting one job well.

Strong AI and Weak AI are two fascinating branches of artificial intelligence that capture our imagination. (A) Strong AI, like something from a sci-fi movie, can think, learn, and perform various tasks and cope with various situations just like humans. (B) The current level of AI systems cannot do such things yet. (C) It can do things such as recommending movies, giving us directions, or even helping us pick the perfect songs. (D) However, it outperforms humans only in the specific tasks it is designed for, and it operates under far more constraints than even the most basic human intelligence. (E) There are several differences between Weak AI and Strong AI.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘반면에, 우리가 현재 매일 접하는 유형인 약한 인공지능은 한 가지 일을 잘 수행하는 데 집중한다.’라는 뜻으로, on the other hand(반면에)를 사용해 강한 인공지능과 대조되는 약한 인공지능의 특징을 소개하는 흐름이므로, 강한 인공지능은 인간처럼 생각하고, 학습하고, 다양한 작업을 수행하며 다양한 상황에 대처할 수 있지만 현재 수준의 인공지능 시스템은 아직 그런 일들을 할 수 없다는 내용의 뒤이자, 주어진 문장의 Weak AI를 It으로 가리켜, 그것이 할 수 있는 일의 구체적인 예로 영화를 추천하거나, 길을 알려주거나, 노래를 선택하는 것을 돕는 것을 제시하는 내용 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in ______. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context in which you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: understanding others’ emotional needs
retaining vast quantities of information
adapting flexibly to unexpected changes
evaluating the importance of information accurately
making ethical judgments in complicated situations
solution:
우리는 모든 답을 암기할 필요가 없다고 했으며, 우리가 집중해야 할 것은 인공지능으로부터 '올바른' 답을 얻는 것이고 그 핵심은 원하는 답을 이끌어 내기 위해 올바른 질문을 하는 것이며, 우리는 현재 모든 세부 사항을 암기하는 것보다 정보를 활용하는 능력이 더 중요한 시대에 있다고 설명하므로, 우리가 아무리 열심히 노력한다 해도 방대한 양의 정보를 외우는 데 있어서 인공지능에 필적할 수 없다는 우리 능력의 한계를 제시한 후 그에 따라 우리에게 필요한 것이 무엇인지 설명하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘방대한 양의 정보를 기억하는 것’이 알맞다.
본문변형 memorizing → retaining
오답
① 다른 사람들의 정서적 욕구를 이해하는 것
③ 예상치 못한 변화에 유연하게 적응하는 것
④ 정보의 중요성을 정확하게 평가하는 것
⑤ 복잡한 상황에서 윤리적 판단을 내리는 것

body:
What Is Weak AI?
Did you know that the computer playing chess and the helpful voice assistant on your phone ⓐare both examples of Weak AI? They may be impressive, but they’re designed for specific tasks and can’t handle anything outside their programming. Weak AI is a category of artificial intelligence confined to a finite domain. By performing operations that require considerable time and ⓑutilizing methods that are not always accessible to people, this technology can be advantageous to society.
It concentrates on tasks such as responding to user input searches or playing games. While it is only as good as its programming and training, Weak AI still helps convert enormous amounts of data into useful information by identifying patterns and generating predictions.
What Is Strong AI?
Strong AI is designed to mimic the cognitive abilities of a human being. It is called “strong” because it has the potential to perform a wide range of tasks, rather than being limited to a specific set of tasks. The more an AI system approaches the abilities of a human being, with all our intelligence, emotion, and broad knowledge, ⓒthe “strong” the AI system is considered.
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI ⓓare that it is designed to learn and adapt to new situations. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system ⓔdesigned to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is that it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is possible to create Strong AI in the future.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ the “strong“ → the “stronger“ (‘the+비교급’ 형태의 The more가 쓰인 앞 절에 콤마(,)로 이어져 ‘~할수록, 더 …하다’라는 뜻의 ‘the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 …’ 표현을 이루어야 하며, 뒤에 이어진 동사구 is considered와 함께 ‘consider+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …인 것으로 여기다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be considered+(to be+)보어(…인 것으로 여겨지다)’를 이루는 보어 역할의 형용사를 써야 하므로, the 뒤에 형용사의 비교급을 사용해 the ”strong“을 the ”stronger“로 고친다.)
ⓓ are → is (주어 One of the key characteristics of Strong AI의 동사 자리에 뒤의 that절을 보어로 취하는 be동사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, ‘one of+복수명사(구)’가 주어일 때 이어지는 동사의 수는 단수인 one에 일치시키므로, 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친다.)
오답
ⓔ 문장의 동사구 can learn에 대한 주어 자리에 쓰인 명사구 a Strong AI system을 수식하는 분사구를 이루어야 하며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘설계된’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘design+목적어+to부정사(구)(~을 …하도록 설계하다)’의 to부정사구(to recognize ~ images)가 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be designed+to부정사(…하도록 설계되다)’의 과거분사 designed는 알맞다.

body:
AI can often find the information we want quickly, but there are problems with this. AI creates a lot of false or (A)[objective / prejudiced] information. Further, AI cannot understand the intentions of the person who created the information, ⓐ그것은 그 정보가 옳은지 그른지를 판단할 능력도 가지고 있지 않다. Moreover, stories of AI providing fake information are often reported. For example, there was a case of a lawyer who submitted non-existent cases made by AI to a real court. There has also been an example of AI recommending restaurants that didn’t exist.
Just as much as misleading information, feeding biased information into AI causes incorrect or even harmful output. A world-famous Internet company had AI study ten years of employee records to create a new employee selection algorithm. However, the company decided to (B)[adopt / give up] the algorithm when it favored men over women. The proportion of male employees was very high and thus the AI’s machine learning had an underlying bias towards male data. When analyzing the information provided by AI, it is always necessary to (C)[assess / trust] the quality of information — remember: garbage in, garbage out.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: prejudiced / give up / trust
objective / adopt / trust
prejudiced / adopt / assess
objective / give up / assess
prejudiced / give up / assess
solution:
(A) 인공지능은 자주 우리가 원하는 정보를 재빠르게 찾을 수 있지만 여기에는 문제가 있다고 했으며, 뒤에서 인공지능이 가짜 정보를 제공한다는 기사가 자주 보도된다고 했으므로, false와 or로 연결되어 틀리거나 편향된 정보를 많이 만들어낸다는 흐름이 되는 prejudiced(편향된, 편파적인)가 알맞다.
objective 객관적인
본문변형 biased → prejudiced
(B) 남성 직원의 비율이 매우 높아 인공지능의 머신 러닝이 남성 데이터에 대한 근본적인 편향을 가지고 있었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 회사가 여성보다 남성을 선호하는 문제점이 있는 인공지능 알고리듬을 포기하기로 결정했다는 흐름이 되는 give up(~을 포기하다)이 알맞다.
adopt ~을 채택하다
본문변형 decided not to use → decided to give up
(C) 편향된 정보를 인공지능에 입력하는 것은 부정확하거나 심지어 해로운 결과를 초래한다고 했으므로, 인공지능이 제공한 정보를 분석할 때 정보의 질을 평가하는 것이 항상 필요하다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 assess(~을 평가하다)가 알맞다.
trust ~을 신뢰하다

solution:
민지가 자신은 영화 버전을 먼저 보고 나면 더 수월하게 느껴진다는 의견에 준호가 한 말이며 뒤에 오늘 밤 그의 집에서 영화 ‘반지의 제왕’을 보자고 제안하는 흐름이므로, ‘I feel the same way.’는 다른 사람의 의견이나 감정에 공감을 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 상대방의 의견에 반대할 때 사용하는 표현인 ② ’내 생각은 좀 달라.‘는 밑줄 친 ⓐ와 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

④ 나도 같은 생각이야.
⑤ 나도 그렇게 느껴.

body:
Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and closing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood ______, making it brave and reckless. Santiago didn’t have much rope left over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth open and teeth shining in the sunlight.
Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower restored. The spear wasn’t very long, too short to hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes flashed and he bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.

The old man could hear the marlin’s skin (A)[healing / tearing] and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, where the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its (B)[resting / struggling].
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He had cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too (C)[long / short]. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. ⓐ잠시 후, 그것은 자신과 함께 창을 가지고 물속으로 천천히 가라앉기 전에, 수면 위에서 가만히 누워 있다.

healing 치유되는
(B) 머리에 창을 찔린 후 상어는 꼬리로 물을 내리쳤고 바닷물을 하얗게 만들었으므로, 그것은 몸부림을 치며 바닷물을 하얗게 만들었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 struggling(몸부림치는 것)이 알맞다.
resting 쉬는 것

“Don’t think, old man,” he said. “Sail on this course and take it when it comes.”
But he couldn’t stop thinking. Alone on the ocean, with the poor marlin’s blood ⓐspilling into the water, all he could do was think. He thought of the great baseball player Joe DiMaggio. He wondered if Joe DiMaggio ⓑcould have killed the shark without losing the spear. Santiago thought of his own injured hands and wondered how Joe DiMaggio could play baseball so well in spite of his own injuries. He wondered ⓒif he, like Joe DiMaggio, could ignore the unbearable pain and fatigue in his body long enough to meet his goals.
“Think about something cheerful, old man,” he said. “Every minute now you are closer to home. You sail lighter for the loss of 40 pounds.”
However, Santiago knew this was false hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these strong ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. ⓓEither fear nor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. He had to come up with a new weapon, ⓔremoved the rowing oars and attaching his knife to one.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But I am not unarmed.”
The breeze got stronger and his boat sped up. He felt fresh, and his determination returned. The sharks would almost certainly take his beautiful marlin, but Santiago would never cease fighting them. (A)______

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓓ Either → Neither (뒤의 nor와 함께 쓰여 ’A도 B도 아닌’이라는 뜻의 상관접속사 ’neither A nor B’ 구조를 이루어야 하므로, Either를 Neither로 고친다.)
ⓔ removed → removing (완전한 절(He ~ weapon)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되어 있으며 문맥상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 주절의 주어와 동일한 의미상 주어인 He가 ‘제거하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 the rowing oars가 이어지고 있으며, 등위접속사 and로 현재분사 attaching와 병렬 연결되어 있으므로 removed는 removing으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 전치사 with, 목적어 the poor marlin’s blood와 함께 ‘~가 …하면서’를 뜻하는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사’ 구문을 이루어야 하며, 명사구인 the poor marlin’s blood가 ‘바다로 쏟아지는’ 주체이며, spill이 ‘쏟아지다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰여 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사구 into the water가 이어지고 있으며 문맥상 ‘피가 쏟아지고 있는’ 진행의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 spilling은 알맞다.

(A) 앞에 있는 명사구 a convention center를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리이며, 수식을 받는 a convention center가 ‘위치해 있는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없어 전치사 in이 바로 이어지고 있으므로, ‘locate A in B(A를 B에 위치시키다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘A be located in B(A가 B에 위치하다)’을 이루는 과거분사 located가 알맞다.
(B) 동사원형 find와 목적어 Canadian and international writers에 이어져 ‘find+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어 사이가 능동적인 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 현재분사를 취할 수 있으며 현재분사인 talking과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 있으므로 현재분사 sharing이 알맞다.
(C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ Copenhagen, Denmark)을 이끌어 선행사인 Humlebaek를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.

Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and closing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood took away the shark’s fear, ⓐmade it brave and reckless. Santiago didn’t have much rope ⓑleft over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth open and teeth shining in the sunlight.
Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower ⓒrestoring. The spear wasn’t very long, too short to hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes flashed and he bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.
The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, ⓓwhere the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He ⓔhad cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, it lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, ⓕtaking the spear with it.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ made → making (동사가 있는 완전한 절(The smell ~ fear)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 또 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로, 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 The smell of blood가 ‘만드는’ 주체이고 뒤에 the shark를 가리키는 목적어 it과 목적격보어 brave and reckless가 이어지고 있으므로 made를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 making으로 고쳐야 한다.)
ⓒ restoring → restored (완전한 절(Santiago’s mind ~ clear) 다음에 접속사가 아닌 콤마(,)로만 이어지고 있으므로 주절과 다른 의미상의 주어가 남아있는 독립분사구문으로, 의미상 주어인 his willpower는 ‘회복되는’ 대상이므로 restoring은 수동의 의미인 과거분사 restored로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 앞의 명사 rope를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리로 수식을 받는 rope가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 left는 알맞다.
ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 완전한 절(the brain was)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 right behind the eyes and above the neck을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계부사 where는 알맞다.
ⓔ 흐름상 그가 창을 던졌던 것은 그가 자신의 창을 빼내려고 했던(tried) 것보다 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거완료(had p.p.)인 had cast는 알맞다.

“Don’t think, old man,” he said. “Sail on this course and take it when it comes.” (A) But he couldn’t stop thinking. (B) Alone on the ocean, with the poor marlin’s blood spilling into the water, all he could do was think. (C) He wondered if Joe DiMaggio could have killed the shark without losing the spear. (D) Santiago thought of his own injured hands and wondered how Joe DiMaggio could play baseball so well in spite of his own injuries. (E) He wondered if he, like Joe DiMaggio, could ignore the unbearable pain and fatigue in his body long enough to ⓐmeet his goals.
“Think about something cheerful, old man,” he said. “Every minute now you are closer to home. You sail lighter for the loss of 40 pounds.”
However, Santiago knew this was ⓑfalse hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these strong ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. Neither fear nor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. He had to ⓒcome up with a new weapon, removing the rowing oars and attaching his knife to one.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But I am not unarmed.”
The breeze got stronger and his boat ⓓsped up. He felt fresh, and his ⓔdetermination returned. The sharks would almost certainly take his beautiful marlin, but Santiago would never cease fighting them. A man can be destroyed, but never defeated.

The Old Man and the Sea is about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t caught a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe cursed. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, far beyond the other fishermen. At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. The fish was so strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. Santiago learned to respect the fish, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. When it finally died, he saw it was too big to put inside the boat. Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and threatened to eat Santiago’s prized fish.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a fisherman’s hard-earned success endangered by a shark
the intensified rivalry between Santiago and the other fishermen
Santiago’s ultimately futile struggle to overcome persistent misfortune
the transformation of a dangerous sea creature into a trusted companion
an old man’s admiration for a magnificent marlin that slipped away from him

Are you keen on exploring the world of literature? Is reading your hobby? Here’s an exciting type of event — literary festivals! These events are hosted in cities with rich literary histories, connecting authors and readers. Take a glance at these festivals across different regions!
Edinburgh International Book Festival
Where: Edinburgh, Scotland
The Edinburgh International Book Festival happens every year in Edinburgh, which was designated the first UNESCO City of Literature. The festival is one of the largest literary events globally and is typically held in August. It takes place at the University of Edinburgh’s College of Art, creating a village atmosphere. There are outdoor screens for live events, making it an engaging experience for all.
Frankfurter Buchmesse
Where: Frankfurt, Germany
The Frankfurter Buchmesse is the world’s largest book fair, drawing together publishers, authors, and book fans from across the globe. It is held for five days in October, with the initial two days usually reserved for trade visitors and professionals, while the following days are open to the general public. This fair is a must for anybody, speaking any language, who has ambitions in the publishing world or simply loves to read.

choices: Exploring the Historical Backgrounds of Literary Festivals

But he couldn’t stop thinking. Alone on the ocean, with the poor marlin’s blood spilling into the water, all he could do was think. He thought of the great baseball player Joe DiMaggio. He wondered if Joe DiMaggio could have killed the shark without losing the spear. Santiago thought of his own injured hands and wondered how Joe DiMaggio could play baseball so well in spite of his own injuries. He wondered if he, like Joe DiMaggio, could ignore the unbearable pain and fatigue in his body long enough to meet his goals.
“ⓐ______, old man,” he said. “Every minute now you are closer to home. You sail lighter for the loss of 40 pounds.”
However, Santiago knew this was false hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these strong ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. Neither fear nor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. ⓑ그는 새로운 무기를 생각해 내야 했고, 배를 젓는 노들을 떼어 (그중) 하나에 자신의 칼을 부착했다.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But I am not unarmed.”
The breeze got stronger and his boat sped up. He felt fresh, and his determination returned. The sharks would almost certainly take his beautiful marlin, but Santiago would never cease fighting them. ⓒA man can be destroyed, but never defeated.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓒA man can be destroyed, but never defeated가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Enduring physical pain always leads to eventual success.
Repeated failures make even the strongest person lose hope.
A wise person always knows exactly when they win or lose.
A person‘s spirit can remain unconquered despite severe physical harm.
Accepting defeat is the best way to avoid unnecessary suffering.
solution: 청새치의 피가 물속으로 쏟아지고 있으며, 물속에는 상어들이 있는 상황에서 Santiago는 손에는 부상을 입었고 창을 잃어버린 상태임에도 계속 싸울 것을 다짐하고 있으며, 상어들에게 청새치를 빼앗길 것임을 알면서도 싸우는 것을 멈추지 않으려는 의지를 보여주고 있으므로, 밑줄 친 ⓒ “인간은 파멸당할 수는 있지만 절대 패배할 수는 없다.”는 청새치를 지키는 과정에서 다치거나 실패함에도 끝까지 맞서려는 정신적인 의지는 꺾이지 않을 수 있다는 의미라고 볼 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 ⓒ가 의미하는 바로 ❹ ‘심각한 신체적 손상에도 불구하고, 사람의 정신은 굴복하지 않은 채로 남을 수 있다.’가 알맞다.

International Book Fair of Bogotá
Where: Bogotá, Colombia
The Bogotá International Book Fair (FILBo) is one of the most important annual events in Colombia. It is held at Corferias, a convention center located in the city of Bogotá. It features a wide range of authors and publishers and highlights Colombian and Latin American literature. It (A)[promotes / restricts] books and literacy through various events for 15 days.
Toronto International Festival of Authors
Where: Toronto, Canada
If you’re in Toronto in September, don’t miss Canada’s oldest literary festival! It’s all about books, authors, and readers coming together. You’ll find Canadian and international writers (B)[sharing / withholding] new stories and talking about writing as an art. Also, if you love mysteries, there’s the Motive Crime & Mystery Festival waiting for you in Toronto as well!
Louisiana Literature Festival
Where: Humlebaek, Denmark
The Louisiana Literature Festival is an annual literary event held in Humlebaek, which is 30 minutes north of Copenhagen, Denmark. It is held around the third weekend of August at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. The festival includes engaging conversations among writers as well as between writers and critics. It also (C)[eliminates / features] readings and diverse performances.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A)        (B)        (C)
choices: promotes    withholding    features
restricts    sharing    features
promotes    sharing    eliminates
restricts    withholding    eliminates
promotes    sharing    features
solution:
(A) 보고타 국제도서전은 특히 다양한 작가와 출판사를 소개하며 콜롬비아와 라틴 아메리카 문학에 주목한다고 했으므로 책과 문해력을 장려한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 promotes(~을 장려하다)가 알맞다.
(B) 토론토 국제 작가 축제는 책과 작가, 독자가 함께 모이는 것에 관한 것이라고 했고, 뒤에 캐나다 및 국제 작가들이 예술로서의 글쓰기에 관해 이야기하고 있는 모습을 보게 될 것이라는 축제의 또 다른 특징이 and(그리고)로 연결되므로, 캐나다 및 국제 작가들이 새로운 이야기를 공유하는 모습을 볼 것이라는 축제의 특징을 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 sharing(~을 공유하는)이 알맞다.
(C) 루이지애나 문학 축제는 작가와 비평가 사이의 대화는 물론 작가들 간의 흥미로운 대화를 포함한다는 축제의 특징을 언급하고 있고 also(또한)로 나열되므로 축제는 또한 낭독회와 다양한 공연을 특색으로 한다는 축제의 또 다른 특징을 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 features(~을 특색으로 하다)가 알맞다.

body:
The Old Man and the Sea ⓐ[is / are] about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t caught a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe ⓑ[cursing / cursed]. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, far beyond the other fishermen. At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. The fish was ⓒ[so / too] strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. Santiago learned to respect the fish, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. When it finally died, he saw (A)______. Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and threatened to eat Santiago’s prized fish.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ        ⓑ        ⓒ
choices: are    cursed    so
is    cursed    so
are    cursing    too
is    cursed    too
is    cursing    so
solution:
ⓐ 주어 The Old Man and the Sea는 작품 제목으로 그 안에 and로 복수의 명사(구)가 포함되어 있더라도 하나의 작품을 나타내어 단수 취급하므로, 단수동사 is가 알맞다.
ⓑ 콤마(,) 앞의 언급된 he(=Santiago)의 상태를 부연 설명하는 분사구로, 의미상 주어인 he가 ‘저주를 받은’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 형태의 형용사 cursed가 알맞다. maybe와 cursed 사이에 he was가 생략된 것으로도 볼 수 있다.
ⓒ 뒤에 오는 형용사와 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days)과 함께 ’너무 ~해서 …하다‘라는 뜻의 ’so+형용사/부사(+that)+주어+동사~‘ 구문을 이루어야 하므로 so가 알맞다.
